title: Spark scoring-server test: cancel jobs, join the job thread, and stop the server in a finally block after the readiness wait
answers: Spark UDF scoring server test hangs or fails on retry after the server never became ready
Why does the Spark pyfunc test leave a background job thread or port bound when wait_server_ready times out?
Where is the cleanup for the Spark job and scoring server handled in tests/pyfunc/test_spark.py?
body:
Path: tests/pyfunc/test_spark.py, the test that starts a scoring server from a Spark job thread (run_job) and then calls ScoringServerClient.wait_server_ready on a fixed port of the shared Spark session.
Rule: Wrap ScoringServerClient.wait_server_ready(timeout=20) in try/finally. In the finally block: spark.sparkContext.cancelAllJobs(), job_thread.join(timeout=60), assert not job_thread.is_alive(), then time.sleep(10) so the server exits and releases the port. Keep the 20-second readiness timeout unchanged.
Symptom: When readiness timed out, the active Spark job, the background job thread and the scoring server kept running. Later retries on the same Spark session and fixed port were contaminated and failed.
Constraints: This is cleanup for leaked work after a readiness failure. It does not fix why server startup is slow. Keep the join bounded and assert on it so a stuck thread fails the test instead of hanging.
applies: Test-only pattern for the Spark scoring-server test in tests/pyfunc/test_spark.py; use the same try/finally shape for similar tests that start a server inside a Spark job thread.
says: Retrying Spark model prediction jobs fails because earlier server ports remain blocked after timeout.
Spark model scoring should clean up background tasks and release ports when startup fails.
Repeated batch scoring runs freeze when a previous prediction server fails to become ready.
search: For Spark scoring-server tests in tests/pyfunc/test_spark.py that start a server in a job thread (run_job), wrap ScoringServerClient.wait_server_ready in a try/finally cleanup block. The finally block must call spark.sparkContext.cancelAllJobs(), join job_thread within 60 seconds, assert it is not alive, and sleep 10 seconds to release the fixed port while keeping the 20-second readiness timeout. This test-only pattern applies to tests/pyfunc/test_spark.py and similar tests starting servers in Spark job threads to clean up leaked resources after readiness timeouts and prevent retry contamination. It does not fix why server startup is slow, and stuck threads must fail bounded joins rather than hanging.
